extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (agents/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for when and how patent examiners may reject claims (including previously allowed claims, final rejections, and first-action finals), and what must be stated or considered in Office actions and replies. Covers use of form paragraphs, IDS effects, RCEs, JRA issues, and applicant reply options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of Previously Allowed Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable may be rejected only after a primary examiner has considered all the facts. An Office action rejecting a previously allowed claim must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great care should be exercised in making such a rejection. When rejecting a previously allowed claim, point out in the Office action that the claim was previously allowed by using Form Paragraph 7.50. See MPEP § 1004 for signature/approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous Action by Different Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: When assigned to act on an application which has received actions by another examiner, the examiner should review the previous search to ensure it is thorough and complete and should not take an entirely new approach or make a new search merely in the hope of finding something.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 904.02. The examiner should avoid reorienting the point of view of a previous examiner or making hasty changes; case law example: Amgen, Inc. v. Hoechst Marion Roussel, Inc., 126 F. Supp. 2d 69 (D. Mass. 2001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.50 (Claims Previously Allowed, Now Rejected)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text: 'The indicated allowability of claim [1] is withdrawn in view of the newly discovered reference(s) to [2]. Rejection(s) based on the newly cited reference(s) follow.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In bracket 2, insert the name(s) of the newly discovered reference. Any action including this form paragraph requires the signature of a Primary Examiner. See MPEP § 1004.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection After Allowance of Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections based on references after allowance are governed by MPEP § 1308.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1308.01 for practice and requirements where a reference is found after allowance of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of Claims Copied From Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims corresponding to claims of a patent are presented in an application, the examiner must determine whether the presented claims are unpatentable on any ground(s) (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, 112, double patenting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any claims in the application are rejectable, they should be rejected. If the ground of rejection is also applicable to the corresponding claims in the patent, any Office action including the rejection must have the approval of the Technology Center Director (see MPEP § 1003). See MPEP Chapter 2300 and 37 CFR Parts 41 and 42 for interferences/derivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Rejection: Statutory Basis and General Requirements (37 CFR 1.113)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the second or any subsequent examination the rejection or other action may be made final; reply to a final rejection is limited (appeal or restricted amendment options). In making such final rejection, the examiner shall repeat or state all grounds of rejection then considered applicable to the claims and clearly state the reasons in support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies must comply with 37 CFR 1.114 (or specified paragraphs), including cancellation of or appeal from each rejected claim. Before making final, develop a clear issue between examiner and applicant; perform thorough first-action search and fully apply references; do not make hasty or ill-considered final rejections; balance speedy conclusion with full and fair hearing for applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Grounds in Final Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: All outstanding grounds of rejection of record should be carefully reviewed and any such grounds relied on in the final rejection should be reiterated and clearly developed so that applicant may readily judge the advisability of an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a single previous Office action contains a complete statement supporting the rejection, the final rejection may refer to that statement but should include rebuttal of any applicant arguments. If appeal is taken, the examiner’s answer should contain a complete statement of position. The final rejection letter should conclude with Form Paragraph 7.39.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.39 (Action Is Final) and 7.39.01 (Pro Se Options)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.39: Standard language notifying applicant that the action is final, reminding of extension of time policy and statutory periods. ¶7.39.01: Final rejection wording tailored for pro se applicants, listing options (appeal, after-final amendment, RCE) and providing resources and links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 7.39.01 must be used when last response was signed only by a pro se applicant. The paragraph explains appeal fees, RCE filing, after-final amendment limitations, advisory actions timing, and abandonment consequences. The Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 should be used in all Office actions up to and including final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments After Final Rejection and Entry Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry of proposed amendments after final rejection is not a matter of right unless the amendment merely cancels claims or complies with a formal requirement made previously. Amendments touching the merits may be admitted upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why they are necessary and why not presented earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an amendment after final does not stop the running of the statutory period for reply unless the examiner holds all claims in condition for allowance. See MPEP §§ 714.12 and 714.13 for post-final amendment practice. An RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 may be filed within the period for reply to withdraw finality where permitted (see MPEP § 706.07(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: When a Final Rejection Is Proper on Second or Subsequent Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Second or subsequent actions on the merits shall be final, except where the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by applicant’s amendment nor based on information submitted in an IDS filed during the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the required fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an IDS with fee is filed within the 1.97(c) period, the examiner may use the information (e.g., a printed publication or evidence of public use) and make the next action final even if claims were not amended, provided no other new ground is introduced. See MPEP § 609.04(b) for IDS specifics. For guidance on what constitutes a new ground, see MPEP § 1207.03(a). Rejections based on art submitted in reply to a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement generally cannot be made final in the next Office action unless necessitated by amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent Claim Treatment in Finality/Rejoinder Situations
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent claim is treated as amended if the independent claim or any claim it references is amended because a dependent claim incorporates all the subject matter of the referenced claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. 112(d) and 37 CFR 1.75. In rejoinder situations (rejoining claims after restriction), the next Office action may be made final if the rejection of rejoined claims was necessitated by applicant’s amendment or an IDS filed during 1.97(c) with fee. See MPEP § 821.04 et seq. for rejoinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of Applicant Amendments That Fail to Show Patentable Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant amends the claims without attempting to show patentable novelty, the examiner should not allow the claims; the claims may be finally rejected if clearly open to rejection on the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraph 7.40 where an action is made final including new grounds of rejection necessitated by applicant’s amendment. Examiners should ensure that applicant had adequate opportunity to avoid all grounds of rejection before making final.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS (37 CFR 1.97(c) with Fee) and Final Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When information is submitted in an information disclosure statement under 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p) during the specified period, the examiner may rely on that information and make the next Office action final, provided no other new ground of rejection unrelated to that IDS is introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraph 7.40.01 when the new ground of rejection was prompted by an IDS with fee; insert the filing date of the IDS in the paragraph. Examiner Note: do not use this when another new ground of rejection (not necessitated by amendment) is also introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Research Agreement (JRA) Prior Art Exception / Disqualification Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s submission invoking the JRA prior art exception under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) (or disqualification under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c)) may prompt a new double patenting rejection necessitated by the exception/disqualification; accordingly, the action may be made final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 7.40.02.aia (AIA-era JRA exception) or 7.40.02.fti (pre-AIA 103(c) disqualification) as appropriate. 7.40.02.aia should only be used for applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia. Insert the filing date of the JRA submission in the paragraph. Do not use if another new ground of rejection not necessitated by amendment or IDS is introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Pre-AIA vs AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103 Rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the only change in a rejection is treating the application as subject to current 35 U.S.C. 102 rather than the pre-AIA version (or vice versa) and the prior art relied upon was prior art under both versions, the subsequent action may be made final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: first action relied on a reference as pre-AIA 102(e) and subsequent action relies on the same reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2); the subsequent action may be final assuming no new requirements or non-prior art rejections were made. Examiners should consider statements of common ownership that may affect applicability of certain references (see MPEP §§ 2146.03 and 2154.02(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: First-Action Final Rejections (Continuations, Substitutes, and RCEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be finally rejected in the first Office action when the new application is a continuing or substitute application and (A) all claims are identical to, patentably indistinct from, or have unity of invention with the claims in the earlier application, and (B) would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if entered earlier. For RCEs, similar criteria apply to the first action after filing the RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is improper to make a first-action final where the continuing/substitute application contains material that was presented in the earlier application after final rejection and denied entry because new issues were raised or new matter issues existed. Also improper in CIP where a claim includes subject matter not present in the earlier application. Requests for interviews prior to first action on a continuing/substitute application should ordinarily be granted. Use Form Paragraphs 7.41 or 7.41.03 when making a first-action final.
